links.title: Tai-otoshi on the IJF technique reference

alt.en: Illustrated sequence of Tai-otoshi, the body drop.

image.source: Compiled club reference document supplied by the project owner; original source not recorded

about.en: A hand throw: tori turns in, extends a leg across uke's shin, and drives uke over it with a strong rotation of the arms and trunk.

en: Your extended leg blocks the shin, carrying no weight
Throw with the hands and hips: it is not a leg lift
Bend the blocking knee, toes gripping the mat
From a right-handed grip, pull your partner's balance forward and to their right front corner, so their weight loads onto their right foot.
Step your left foot back and across behind you, turning your body side-on to them; you do not make back contact in this throw.
Extend your right leg across the front of their right shin, your foot planted just outside their ankle, knee bent, toes gripping the mat. The leg is a bar; it carries none of their weight.
Pull the sleeve hard past your left hip and drive the lapel hand across their chest, rotating your whole trunk to the left.
Their body rotates over the barred shin and they land on their back in front of you and to your left. Release the rotation only when the sleeve has guided them down.

receiving.en: Your partner turns and draws you forward, bars your shin with a straight leg, and keeps turning your upper body over it. The fall is a clean forward rotation. Keep your chin tucked and swing your left arm ready; you land on your back past their leg, sleeve still held, left arm slapping.

viNotes.en: There is no back contact here, which takes away the checkpoint most turning throws give you. Use the leg instead: slide your foot out along the mat until it plants just outside their ankle, so the bar is placed by contact and the distance is known rather than guessed. Their weight loading the front foot is the cue to turn, and the throw itself is the rotation of both hands.

cue.en: The attacker turns in and extends a leg across the opponent's shin; the opponent is driven over it fast and flat.
